newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Ex-Nicaraguan rebel advises cool heads in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Nicaraguan rebel advises cool heads in Peru.

text.p: Negotiation is the only way to end the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru, a former Sandinista guerrilla leader who carried out a similar assault in 1978 said on Friday.

"This type of situation demands the calm and serenity of all the parties involved," said Dora Maria Tellez, who fought as Commander Two in the 1970s. "I see no other solution than negotiation, because anything else would risk many lives."

Tellez was second-in-command under legendary guerrilla leader Eden Pastora, Commander Zero, in the dramatic 1978 assault on Nicaragua's National Palace where more than 200 lawmakers and ministers were held hostage for 54 hours before being freed without casualties.

Analysts here have said the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels in Peru were copying the Sandinistas' 1978 assault, even though Tellez told reporters the two hostage-takings took place in different historical contexts.
"Militarily speaking (the MRTA's assault) was a super operation. An operation like that takes at least a year and a half to plan," she said.

In the Sandinista assault on the National Palace, part of their efforts to topple longtime dictator Anastasio Somoza, the rebels succeeded in negotiating the release of 40 to 50 imprisoned fellow guerrillas, including top commander Tomas Borge, who later became Sandinista Interior Minister after the 1979 overthrow of Somoza, Tellez said.
Tellez is currently a congresswoman for the Sandinista Renovation Movement in Nicaragua, and has a business selling Christmas trees.
